gloss: turn; go round; surround; all around
summary: The root is motion or position in a circle about a point. The verb is to turn (oneself, one's face, a thing), to go round a place or about in it, and to surround, whether as an enemy closing in or as Yahweh guarding his own; in the hiphil it is to turn a thing another way, to bring it round, or to turn it over to another, as the kingdom was turned to David. סָבִיב, two thirds of the root's uses, is “all around, on every side”: of the blood splashed on the altar all around, of the camp around the Dwelling, of the nations around Israel, of the rest Yahweh gives “from all around”, and of the measurements of Ezekiel's house. A turn of events is a סִבָּה, and scripture says of the dividing of the kingdom that “the turn was from Yahweh”.

words.gloss: all around, on every side; around; surroundings
words.summary: A noun in form, “a going round, circuit”, but nearly always used as an adverb (“all around”) or, with לְ or in the plural construct סְבִיבוֹת and with suffixes (סְבִיבֹתָיו, סְבִיבָיו), as a preposition (“around”). With מִן, מִסָּבִיב is “from every side” or simply “on every side”. The plural, masculine or feminine, is also a noun: the places or the people around. More than a hundred of its uses are in Ezekiel, most of them in the measuring of the house (Ezk 40 to 43), and many more are in the making of the tabernacle and the temple.

senses.gloss: all around, on every side (adverb)
senses.definition: Standing after its verb or noun without a preposition: on all sides of the thing spoken of, the whole way round it. So of a border, a wall, a court or a rim that runs round, of what is done to every side of a thing, and of looking or standing in every direction.

evidence.note: “You shall set bounds for the people סָבִיב”: a boundary on every side of the mountain, so that none could touch it from any quarter.
“Have you not hedged about him, and about his house, and about all that is his, מִסָּבִיב?”: the hedge is on every side, leaving no gap.
The ark: “you shall make on it a border of gold סָבִיב”.
The priests “shall splash the blood on the altar סָבִיב”: on all its sides. So of every burnt offering, peace offering and guilt offering (Lev 1:11; 3:2; 7:2).
The blood of the bull and of the goat put “on the horns of the altar סָבִיב”.
Every tree in the field of Machpelah, “in all its border סָבִיב”.
Villages “which have no wall סָבִיב”.
The side chambers built against the walls of the house סָבִיב, three times in the verse.
The cast sea, “round סָבִיב … and a line of thirty cubits would go round it סָבִיב”: the adverb beside the verb יָסֹב.
Gideon's men “stood each in his place סָבִיב לַמַּחֲנֶה”.
“Lift up your eyes סָבִיב and see”: in every direction (so Isa 60:4).
“He breaks me down סָבִיב, and I am gone.”
“I will be to her a wall of fire סָבִיב, and glory in her midst.”
The rims of the wheels “full of eyes סָבִיב, the four of them” (so Ezk 10:12).

senses.gloss: סָבִיב סָבִיב: all the way round
senses.definition: The word doubled, almost only in Ezekiel's vision of the house: round on every side, the whole circuit, of walls, chambers, windows, borders and measurements.

evidence.note: “A wall outside the house סָבִיב סָבִיב”: the wall enclosing the whole.
“To the four winds he measured it; it had a wall סָבִיב סָבִיב, five hundred long and five hundred wide”: the four sides are the “around, around”.
“This is the law of the house: on the top of the mountain all its border סָבִיב סָבִיב is most holy.”
“He made me pass by them סָבִיב סָבִיב”: all round the bones of the valley.
The side chambers “סָבִיב סָבִיב to the house סָבִיב”.
The oxen under the sea “סָבִיב סָבִיב going round it”.

senses.gloss: מִסָּבִיב: from every side; on every side
senses.definition: With מִן: from all the quarters around, of enemies, terror, reproach or the gathering of the scattered coming in from every side; and of rest or deliverance from the enemies on every side. Often it is no more than “on every side”.

evidence.note: “Yahweh gave them rest מִסָּבִיב … not a man of all their enemies stood before them”: the rest is from the enemies on every side.
“Do not go out to the field nor walk on the road, for the enemy has a sword: מָגוֹר מִסָּבִיב”: terror from every side, so that no way out is safe.
“He will give you rest from all your enemies מִסָּבִיב, and you will dwell in safety.”
Yahweh “delivered them from the hand of all their enemies מִסָּבִיב”.
“Yahweh had given him rest מִסָּבִיב from all his enemies.”
Solomon “had peace from all his sides מִסָּבִיב”.
“I will gather them against you מִסָּבִיב.”
“I will gather them מִסָּבִיב and bring them to their own soil.”
The birds and beasts called to “assemble מִסָּבִיב to my sacrifice”.
The heat of his anger “set him on fire מִסָּבִיב, and he did not know”.
“There I will sit to judge all the nations מִסָּבִיב.”
“You have called, as on a day of appointed feast, my terrors מִסָּבִיב.”

senses.gloss: around (preposition)
senses.definition: Governing a noun or a suffix: in a ring about a person, place or thing. It is formed three ways: סָבִיב לְ, the plural construct סְבִיבוֹת, and the plural with a suffix (סְבִיבֹתָיו, סְבִיבָיו “around him”).

evidence.note: The Levites “shall encamp סָבִיב לַמִּשְׁכָּן”; Num 2:2 has the tribes encamp “סָבִיב לְאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד” at a distance: two rings with the Dwelling at the centre.
“The angel of Yahweh encamps סָבִיב לִירֵאָיו and rescues them.”
“Jerusalem: mountains are סָבִיב לָהּ, and Yahweh is סָבִיב לְעַמּוֹ”: as the hills stand round the city, so he round his people.
“The hill was full of horses and chariots of fire סְבִיבֹת אֱלִישָׁע.”
“A layer of dew סָבִיב לַמַּחֲנֶה.”
The Egyptians dug סְבִיבֹת הַיְאֹר for water to drink.
Moses stood the seventy elders סְבִיבֹת הָאֹהֶל.
Saul lay within the camp “and the people were encamped סְבִיבֹתָיו”.
“Cloud and thick darkness are סְבִיבָיו.”
“A fire devours before him, and סְבִיבָיו it storms greatly.”
“Your sons like olive shoots סָבִיב לְשֻׁלְחָנֶךָ.”
Solomon's litter, “sixty mighty men סָבִיב לָהּ”.
“The nations that are סְבִיבֹתֵיכֶם”: so Deu 6:14, “the gods of the peoples who are סְבִיבוֹתֵיכֶם”.
“This is Jerusalem: I set her in the midst of the nations, and lands are סְבִיבוֹתֶיהָ.”

senses.gloss: surroundings: the places or people around; circuit
senses.definition: As a noun, mostly plural: the country round a place (its environs), the people or nations round a person or people (neighbours), and once each the circuits of the wind and the surrounding part of a city.

evidence.note: Fields will be bought “in the land of Benjamin, and in סְבִיבֵי יְרוּשָׁלִַם, and in the cities of Judah”: the environs of Jerusalem listed as a district among districts (so Jer 33:13; 17:26).
“Let all סְבִיבָיו bring a gift to the one to be feared”: “those around him” as the subject of a verb.
“Bemoan him, all סְבִיבָיו, and all who know his name.”
God is “feared above all סְבִיבָיו”.
“A scorn and derision to סְבִיבוֹתֵינוּ”, beside “our neighbours” (שְׁכֵנֵינוּ); so Psa 79:4.
“Jerusalem and your people are a reproach to all סְבִיבֹתֵינוּ.”
“All סְבִיבֹתֵיהֶם strengthened their hands with vessels of silver.”
The fire “will devour all סְבִיבֶיהָ”.
“This assembly will lick up all סְבִיבֹתֵינוּ, as the ox licks up the green of the field.”
“I will make them and סְבִיבוֹת גִּבְעָתִי a blessing.”
“Going round, going round, the wind goes, and on סְבִיבֹתָיו the wind returns”: its rounds, the noun beside the verb three times in the verse.
David “built the city מִסָּבִיב, from the Millo and to הַסָּבִיב”: the only use with the article, the surrounding part.
“κύκλῳ the throne, four living creatures full of eyes before and behind”: the living creatures and the eyes of Ezk 1:18 and 10:12.
“All the angels stood κύκλῳ the throne.”
“A rainbow κυκλόθεν the throne”: as the brightness all around was like the bow in the cloud (Ezk 1:28).
The four living creatures “κυκλόθεν and within full of eyes” (Ezk 1:18; 10:12).

opposites.note: What is around is set against what is in the midst: Jerusalem in the midst of the nations with lands around her; a wall of fire around and glory in the midst.

evidence.note: Brightness around the cloud, and from its midst the gleam.

phrases.gloss: terror on every side: Jeremiah's cry, and the name he gave Pashhur

evidence.note: “Yahweh has not called your name Pashhur but מָגוֹר מִסָּבִיב.”

phrases.gloss: give rest from all around (from the enemies on every side)
the nations that are around you

evidence.note: “The peoples who are around you”, whose gods Israel must not follow.

phrases.gloss: on the altar all around: where the blood of an offering is splashed

words.gloss: turn; go round, go about; surround
words.summary: About 160 times. The qal and niphal are mostly intransitive (turn, go round, close round), the hiphil causative (turn a thing, bring it round, turn it over), and the poel is to go about or to encompass. Whether the sense is “turn” or “go round” or “surround” is shown by what follows: a direction or a person turned from or to; a city, land or mountain gone round; a person or house closed in on (often with עַל).

stems.gloss: turn; go round, go about; surround; come round to

senses.gloss: turn, turn round, turn aside
senses.definition: To change the way one faces or goes: to turn round, turn away from one person and toward another, turn aside, turn back. Of the Jordan it is to turn backward; of a door, to turn on its hinge.

evidence.note: Joseph “וַיִּסֹּב from them and wept, and returned to them”: he turned his back so that they should not see.
“The door תִּסּוֹב on its hinge, and the sluggard on his bed”: turning about a fixed point without going anywhere.
“The sea saw and fled; the Jordan יִסֹּב לְאָחוֹר”: turned backward, beside “fled”.
“Samuel וַיִּסֹּב to go”, and Saul seized the edge of his robe.
David “וַיִּסֹּב from beside him toward another”.
“David וַיִּסֹּב from before him twice”: he turned out of the way of the spear.
“סֹב you, and fall on the priests; and Doeg the Edomite וַיִּסֹּב and fell on the priests.”
“סֹב, stand here; וַיִּסֹּב and stood.”
Jehu to the rider: “סֹב behind me.”
“Let him יִסֹּב to his house, and my face he shall not see.”
The captives “וַיָּסֹבּוּ and returned and went to Johanan”.
“סֹב, be like a gazelle, my beloved.”
“וְסַבּוֹתִי I, to make my heart despair”: of the mind turning to a new thought (so Ecc 7:25).
“You will increase my greatness, וְתִסֹּב, you will comfort me”: turn again.

senses.gloss: go round, make a circuit; go about
senses.definition: To travel round a place: right round it, as Israel round Jericho; round the outside of it so as not to enter, as round Edom; or about within it from place to place, as Samuel on his yearly round and the watchmen in the city. Of a river, to run round or through a land; of a measuring line, to go round a pillar.

evidence.note: “וְסַבֹּתֶם the city, all the men of war, going round (הַקֵּיף) the city once”: explained by the verb beside it. On the seventh day seven times (Jos 6:4, 15).
“By the way of the Sea of Reeds לִסְבֹב the land of Edom”: to pass round it, because Edom refused the way through (so Jdg 11:18; Deu 2:1, 3).
Samuel “went year by year וְסָבַב Bethel and Gilgal and Mizpah, and judged Israel in all these places”: a round of places, ending where it began (verse 17, “his return was to Ramah”).
The Pishon “is the one הַסֹּבֵב all the land of Havilah”; the Gihon likewise the land of Cush (Gen 2:13).
“סֹבּוּ Zion and go round her (וְהַקִּיפוּהָ); count her towers.”
The three kings “וַיָּסֹבּוּ a way of seven days”.
“The watchmen הַסֹּבְבִים in the city found me.”
“The mourners וְסָבְבוּ in the street.”
The teachers “וַיָּסֹבּוּ in all the cities of Judah and taught the people”.
“Take a harp, סֹבִּי the city, forgotten harlot.”
The wind “goes to the south וְסוֹבֵב to the north; סוֹבֵב סֹבֵב the wind goes, and on its circuits the wind returns”.
“A line of twelve cubits יָסֹב the second pillar”: its measure round (so 1Ki 7:23; Jer 52:21).
“Send and fetch him, for לֹא נָסֹב until he comes here”: we will not take our places round (the meal); compare מֵסַב in Sng 1:12.

senses.gloss: surround, close in on
senses.definition: To be or come on every side of a person or place. Mostly of enemies: men round a house or a city, an army round its prey, and in the psalms bulls, dogs, bees, waters and the cords of the grave round the sufferer. Also of things that simply stand round: sheaves, willows, a man's own deeds.

evidence.note: “Behold, an army סוֹבֵב the city, and horses and chariots”: the city is shut in, and the servant says, “what shall we do?”
“All nations סְבָבוּנִי”; verse 11, “סַבּוּנִי, yes סְבָבוּנִי”; verse 12, “סַבּוּנִי like bees”.
“Dogs סְבָבוּנִי; a company of evildoers have encircled me (הִקִּיפוּנִי)”: the two verbs say the same.
“Many bulls סְבָבוּנִי; strong ones of Bashan have ringed me (כִּתְּרוּנִי).”
“The cords of the grave סְבָבוּנִי; the snares of death were before me” (so 2Sa 22:6).
“They סַבּוּנִי like water all the day; they have closed in (הִקִּיפוּ) on me together.”
The Gazites “וַיָּסֹבּוּ and lay in wait for him all night at the gate”.
“The lords of Gibeah וַיָּסֹבּוּ against me the house by night.”
“Ten young men וַיָּסֹבּוּ and struck Absalom and killed him.”
“A great king came against it וְסָבַב it and built great siege works against it.”
David could not build “because of the war with which they סְבָבֻהוּ”.
“Ephraim סְבָבֻנִי with lying.”
“Now their deeds סְבָבוּם; they are before my face.”
“Your sheaves תְסֻבֶּינָה and bowed down to my sheaf.”
“The willows of the brook יְסֻבּוּהוּ.”

senses.gloss: come round to, pass over to; bring about
senses.definition: Of a thing that changes hands or place: to go round to another. So of the ark sent on from city to city, an inheritance passing from tribe to tribe, the kingdom passing from Adonijah to Solomon, and the cup of Yahweh's right hand coming round to the drinker. Once, of a man, to have brought a thing about.

evidence.note: Adonijah: “the kingdom was mine … וַתִּסֹּב the kingdom and became my brother's, for it was his from Yahweh.”
“An inheritance of the sons of Israel shall not תִסֹּב from tribe to tribe; each shall cleave to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers”: to go round is the opposite of to cleave (so Num 36:9).
“Let the ark of the God of Israel יִסֹּב to Gath.”
“The cup of Yahweh's right hand תִּסּוֹב upon you.”
David to Abiathar: “I סַבֹּתִי against every soul of your father's house”: I have been the occasion of their death. The only such use; compare סִבָּה.

stems.gloss: turn (a thing); bring round, lead round; turn over to; change (a name); set round

senses.gloss: turn (the face, the heart, the eyes)
senses.definition: To make a part of oneself or of another face a different way: the face toward or away from someone, the eyes away, the heart of a people back to God or of a king toward his people.

evidence.note: Hezekiah “וַיַּסֵּב his face to the wall and prayed to Yahweh” (so Isa 38:2).
“The king וַיַּסֵּב his face and blessed all the assembly of Israel”: from the house toward the people standing behind him.
“That this people may know that you, Yahweh, are God, and that you הֲסִבֹּתָ their heart back again.”
Yahweh “וְהֵסֵב the heart of the king of Assyria to them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of God”.
“Our fathers … וַיַּסֵּבּוּ their faces from the dwelling of Yahweh and gave the back.”
“וַהֲסִבּוֹתִי my face from them.”
Ahab “lay on his bed וַיַּסֵּב his face and ate no bread”.
The sons of Dan “וַיַּסֵּבּוּ their faces”.
“הָסֵבִּי your eyes from before me.”
“Josiah did not הֵסֵב his face from him.”

senses.gloss: bring round, lead round, carry round; take a way round
senses.definition: To make a person or thing go round: the ark round Jericho, the people round by the wilderness road, the ark from city to city; and, with no object, to take a way round behind an enemy. Also to move a thing aside out of its place.

evidence.note: “וַיַּסֵּב the ark of Yahweh round the city, going round once”: the causative of the qal of Jos 6:3.
God did not lead them by the near way of the Philistines, “וַיַּסֵּב אֱלֹהִים the people by the way of the wilderness of the Sea of Reeds”: the long way round.
“וַיַּסֵּבּוּ the ark of the God of Israel” to Gath; verse 10, “הֵסַבּוּ to me the ark … to kill me and my people”.
“You shall not go up; הָסֵב to their rear and come on them opposite the balsam trees” (so 1Ch 14:14).
“Jeroboam הֵסֵב the ambush to come from behind them.”
“וַיְסִבֵּנִי by the way outside to the outer gate.”
“וַיַּסֵּב Amasa from the highway into the field.”
The covered way of the sabbath “הֵסֵב from the house of Yahweh”.
“וְנָסֵבָּה the ark of our God to us.”
“Behold, I am מֵסֵב the weapons of war that are in your hand.”

senses.gloss: turn over to another; change (a name)
senses.definition: To make a thing another's or another thing: the kingdom turned from Saul to David, all Israel brought over to him, and a king's name changed by the overlord who set him up.

evidence.note: Saul “did not seek Yahweh, and he killed him וַיַּסֵּב the kingdom to David son of Jesse”.
They came to Hebron “לְהָסֵב the kingdom of Saul to him, according to the mouth of Yahweh”.
Abner: “my hand is with you לְהָסֵב to you all Israel.”
Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim king “וַיַּסֵּב his name to Jehoiakim” (so 2Ch 36:4).
The king of Babylon made Mattaniah king “וַיַּסֵּב his name to Zedekiah”.

senses.gloss: set round, surround with
senses.definition: To put a wall round a place.

evidence.note: “Let us build these cities וְנָסֵב wall and towers, doors and bars.”

stems.gloss: close round; turn (of a border, of the living creatures); be turned over to

senses.gloss: close round, gather round against
senses.definition: With עַל: to draw in on every side of a house or a people, as the men of Sodom and of Gibeah did.

evidence.note: “The men of Sodom נָסַבּוּ עַל הַבַּיִת, from young to old, all the people from every quarter.”
The men of Gibeah “נָסַבּוּ the house, beating on the door”.
“The Canaanite will hear וְנָסַבּוּ עָלֵינוּ and cut off our name from the earth.”

senses.gloss: turn, bend round (of a border; of going)
senses.definition: To leave the straight line: of a boundary, to bend from one point toward another; of the living creatures and their wheels, which did not turn as they went.

evidence.note: “They did not יִסַּבּוּ as they went; each went straight before his face”: to turn is the opposite of going straight ahead (so Ezk 1:12, 17; 10:11, 16).
“The border וְנָסַב for you from the south of the ascent of Akrabbim and passes on to Zin”; verse 5, “וְנָסַב from Azmon to the brook of Egypt”.
“The border וְנָסַב from Baalah westward to Mount Seir.”
“The border was drawn וְנָסַב to the west side southward.”
The measuring line goes out over the hill Gareb “וְנָסַב to Goah”.
The side chambers widened “וְנָסְבָה upward and upward”: winding up round the house.

senses.gloss: be turned over to another
senses.definition: The passive of the qal “pass over to”: of houses, fields and a city's trade passing into other hands.

evidence.note: “Their houses וְנָסַבּוּ to others, fields and wives together.”
Tyre of Jerusalem: “the doors of the peoples are broken; נָסֵבָּה to me; I shall be filled.”

senses.gloss: go about (in a city), go round (the altar)
senses.definition: To walk round or about a place: the seeker in the streets, the wicked on the walls and round the city like dogs, the worshipper round Yahweh's altar.

evidence.note: “I will rise וַאֲסוֹבְבָה in the city, in the streets and in the squares; I will seek him whom my soul loves.”
“They return at evening, they howl like a dog וִיסוֹבְבוּ the city” (so verse 15).
“Day and night יְסוֹבְבֻהָ on her walls, and iniquity and trouble are within her.”
“I wash my hands in innocence וַאֲסֹבְבָה your altar, Yahweh.”

senses.gloss: encompass (to guard, or to overwhelm)
senses.definition: To be all round a person. Of Yahweh's care for Israel and for the one who trusts him; of the waters of the deep round Jonah.

evidence.note: “He found him in a wilderness land … יְסֹבְבֶנְהוּ, he cared for him, he kept him as the pupil of his eye”: the three verbs together are guarding.
“He who trusts in Yahweh, faithful love יְסוֹבְבֶנּוּ”; verse 7, “with songs of deliverance תְּסוֹבְבֵנִי”.
“You cast me into the deep … and the flood יְסֹבְבֵנִי”; verse 6, “the deep יְסֹבְבֵנִי”.
“The assembly of peoples תְּסוֹבְבֶךָּ.”
“Yahweh has created a new thing in the land: a female תְּסוֹבֵב a man.” The verb is plain; what the saying refers to is not explained in the passage.

stems.gloss: be set round; be turned, be rolled; be changed (of a name)

senses.gloss: be set round (with gold)
senses.definition: The participle, of the stones of the ephod and the breastplate enclosed in settings of gold.

evidence.note: The two onyx stones “מֻסַבֹּת settings of gold you shall make them” (so Exo 39:6, 13).

senses.gloss: be turned, be rolled; be changed
senses.definition: Of a cart wheel rolled over grain, of the leaves of a door that turn, and of the names of cities that were changed.

evidence.note: “Nor is a cart wheel יוּסָּב over cumin.”
“Two leaves to the doors, two מוּסַבּוֹת leaves”: leaves that turn.
Nebo and Baal Meon, “מוּסַבֹּת שֵׁם”: their names being changed; compare the hiphil of 2Ki 23:34.

senses.gloss: change (the face of a matter)
senses.definition: Once: to make a matter look other than it did.

evidence.note: The woman of Tekoa: “in order to סַבֵּב the face of the matter your servant Joab has done this thing.”
“By faith the walls of Jericho fell, having been encircled (κυκλωθέντα) seven days”: the going round of Jos 6.
“When you see Jerusalem being surrounded (κυκλουμένην) by armies, then know that her desolation has come near.”
“The Jews surrounded (ἐκύκλωσαν) him” in the temple, and then took up stones.
“They surrounded (ἐκύκλωσαν) the camp of the saints and the beloved city.”

parallels.note: The hiphil of נקף, “go round, encircle”, stands beside סָבַב both of marching round a city and of enemies closing in.
“Close over”: waters closed over Jonah as the deep was round him.
“Turn (the face) toward”: Israel turned and journeyed, and went round Mount Seir; “enough of going round this mountain: turn north”.
“Return”: the wind goes round and returns on its circuits; the captives turned round and returned.

opposites.note: An inheritance is not to go round from tribe to tribe: each is to cleave to his own.
The living creatures did not turn: each went אֶל עֵבֶר פָּנָיו, straight before its face.

phrases.gloss: go round the city: the march round Jericho

words.gloss: what is round about; a round (of those at table)
words.summary: Five uses, in four different forms, so that each rests on little. Three are “round about” or “the parts round about”, as סָבִיב is used; one is the king's “round” in the Song, where he sits or reclines; and מְסִבָּי in Psa 140:10 may be this noun (“those round me”) or the hiphil participle of the verb (“those who surround me”): the sense is the same either way.

senses.gloss: round about; the parts round about; those round about
senses.definition: What surrounds: used as an adverb of walls carved all round, as a noun of the country round Jerusalem and of the enemies round the psalmist, and in the feminine plural of the cloud turning round and round.

evidence.note: “All the walls of the house מֵסַב he carved with carved figures of cherubim and palm trees”: where 1Ki 6:5 has סָבִיב.
The priests who burned incense “in the cities of Judah וּמְסִבֵּי יְרוּשָׁלִָם”: as סְבִיבֵי יְרוּשָׁלִַם in Jer 32:44.
“The head of מְסִבָּי: let the mischief of their lips cover them.”
The cloud “turns itself מְסִבּוֹת by his guidance, to do all that he commands”.

senses.gloss: a round of those at table; a couch
senses.definition: Once: where the king is while the nard gives its scent, taken to be the circle in which he and his company sit or recline at a meal.

evidence.note: “While the king was בִּמְסִבּוֹ, my nard gave its scent.” The verse does not say what the מֵסַב is; 1Sa 16:11, “we will not נָסֹב until he comes”, of sitting down to the sacrificial meal, is the nearest light on it.

words.summary: Once only, so its sense rests on one verse and on the verb. The Chronicler's parallel has נְסִבָּה in its place.

senses.gloss: a turn of events, brought about by Yahweh
senses.definition: The way a matter turned: Rehoboam's refusal of the people, by which the kingdom passed from him. The verb is used of the same thing, the kingdom that “turned” and became another's.

evidence.note: “The king did not listen to the people, for it was a סִבָּה from Yahweh, in order to establish his word which Yahweh spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam.”
The verb of the same matter a generation before: “the kingdom turned (וַתִּסֹּב) and became my brother's, for it was his from Yahweh.”

words.summary: Once only, in the Chronicler's telling of 1Ki 12:15, where Kings has סִבָּה: the same sense in a noun shaped from the niphal, “a thing turned”.

senses.gloss: a turn of events, brought about by God
senses.definition: As סִבָּה: the turn the matter took when Rehoboam refused the people.

evidence.note: “The king did not listen to the people, for it was a נְסִבָּה from God, in order that Yahweh might establish his word.”

words.gloss: a winding round, surround (of the house)
words.summary: Once only, in a hard verse of Ezekiel's house, so that its sense is not fixed: what goes round the house and rises with the side chambers, storey by storey.

senses.gloss: what winds or goes round (the house)
senses.definition: Named beside the niphal of the verb and the doubled סָבִיב in the same verse: the structure that went round the house, higher and wider at each storey.

evidence.note: “It widened and wound (וְנָסְבָה) upward and upward for the side chambers, for the מוּסַב of the house was upward and upward סָבִיב סָבִיב to the house.”

cognates.note: The same root with the same weak forms as the Hebrew: the imperfect ysb beside Hebrew יָסֹב.

evidence.locator: p. 73, §54.56, Verbs II = III: G imperfect 3 m. ysb /yasubbu/; “/s-b-b/ ‘to turn’”
evidence.note: From the table of characteristic forms and the list of roots beneath it (OCR read; PDF not rendered). The glossary to the selected texts has no entry for the root.
“Compare Ugaritic 𐎒𐎁 (sb /sabba/, ‘to turn’).”

cognates.gloss: surround, encircle (as an enemy); (yiphil) turn over, hand over
cognates.note: Both halves of the Hebrew verb. In a Neo-Punic text in Latin letters a militia “surrounded” a place before its enemy was taken, as armies surround a city in Hebrew; in the Phoenician of Cebel Ires Dağı a king “turned over” fields, and a woman was “turned over” to another man, with the causative as Hebrew has it of the kingdom turned over to David (1Ch 10:14).

evidence.note: “[Heb. s-b-b] v. qal SURROUND, ENCIRCLE in a hostile sense: Dreder 6.8/9 (NPu) Sab siben Mycne, ‘Our militia surrounded Mycne’ … v. yiphʿil 1. TURN OVER, RETURN something/someone: CID, lines 7AB–8AB (Ph) … ‘the king of WRYKLY turned over all these fields’” (read from the extracted text; PDF not rendered).

cognates.note: Rare in Aramaic, whose ordinary verb for “go round, surround” is סְחַר: the Targum renders the סָבַב of Jos 6 by it. That is why no word of this root is found in the Aramaic of Daniel and Ezra or in the Peshitta.

evidence.locator: s.v. סְבַב (ch.), “same” as סָבַב; Af. אַסִּב
evidence.note: “to go around (announcing). Y. R. Hash. II, 58ᵃ top … these went around (as messengers to announce the New-Moon) to-day, and others the day after.”

evidence.locator: s.v. סְחַר, “to go around, turn (corresp. to h. סָבַב)”; Af. “to surround, enclose. Targ. Josh. VI, 3; 11; 14”
evidence.note: The Aramaic verb that stands where Hebrew has סָבַב.

cognates.gloss: the ledge running round the altar (Jewish Aramaic)
cognates.note: Onkelos' word for the כַּרְכֹּב of the bronze altar, the ledge that ran round it halfway up (Exo 27:5; 38:4): a noun for a thing that goes round, as סָבִיב and מֵסַב are.

evidence.note: “Targ. O. Ex. XXVII, 5 … (h. text כרכב). Ib. XXXVIII, 4.”

cognates.note: The Targum's word in Ezk 41:7, the verse of מוּסָב and וְנָסְבָה, and for the לוּלִים by which one went up to the middle storey in 1Ki 6:8: a stair that winds round.

evidence.note: “winding staircase. Targ. Ez. XLI, 7 (h. text נסבה!). Pl. … Targ. I Kings VI, 8 (h. text לולים).”

cognates.gloss: rope; a means of reaching a thing; a cause, occasion
cognates.note: Arabic has no verb of this root meaning “turn” or “go round”; its verb sabba is “cut” and “revile”. But sabab, a rope and so a means and a cause, with sabbaba “make a means or cause, occasion”, answers in sense to סִבָּה, the turn of events that was “from Yahweh”, and to David's “I have brought it about” (1Sa 22:22). Whether the Arabic noun belongs to the root of going round (a rope as a thing wound) or is a separate word is not shown, so it is kept as possible only.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1285, art. سب, سَبَبٌ
evidence.note: “A rope, or cord … Hence, a thing of any kind by means of which one attains, reaches, or gains access to another thing … a means by which a thing is brought about: a cause … an occasion, or accidental cause.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1284, art. سب, form 2 سَبَّبَ
evidence.note: “He made, or appointed, or prepared, a means, or cause, of attaining, or accomplishing, the thing … [And سبّب, alone, He, or it, caused, or occasioned.]”

cognates.note: A single Sabaic use, “a brawl took place between the two”, set beside the Arabic sabbaba “bring about”. It is the sense of סִבָּה and נְסִבָּה, a thing that comes about; one use is too little to build on.

evidence.note: “pf sb J700/10. COME ABOUT, TAKE PLACE [Cf Ar sbb D ‘bring about, cause to arise.’] J700/10: wsb bynhmw lḫmm ‘a brawl took place between the 2’” (OCR read).

doctrine.statement: When Rehoboam answered the people roughly and the ten tribes left him, the writer says “the king did not listen to the people, for it was a turn (סִבָּה) from Yahweh, to establish his word which Yahweh spoke by Ahijah” (1Ki 12:15; 2Ch 10:15). Adonijah said the same of Solomon's throne: “the kingdom turned and became my brother's, for it was his from Yahweh” (1Ki 2:15); and of Saul it is written that Yahweh “killed him and turned the kingdom to David” (1Ch 10:14). Elijah prayed that the people might know “that you have turned their heart back again” (1Ki 18:37), and the returned exiles kept the feast with joy because Yahweh “had turned the heart of the king of Assyria to them” (Ezr 6:22). In each case men acted as they chose (Rehoboam took the counsel he liked, 1Ki 12:8), and yet the outcome is called Yahweh's. From the verses: the turns of kingdoms and of kings' hearts are in his hand, as Proverbs says, “the heart of a king is in the hand of Yahweh as channels of water; he turns it wherever he will” (Pro 21:1), and as Nebuchadnezzar was made to learn, “the Most High rules in the kingdom of men and gives it to whom he will” (Dan 4:14).

“The angel of Yahweh encamps around those who fear him and rescues them” (Psa 34:8). When the army of Aram surrounded (סוֹבֵב) Dothan to take Elisha, his servant saw only the army; Elisha prayed, Yahweh opened the young man's eyes, “and behold, the hill was full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisha” (2Ki 6:15–17). The psalm says as much of Yahweh himself: “as the mountains are around Jerusalem, Yahweh is around his people, from now and for ever” (Psa 125:2); and of Israel in the wilderness, “he encompassed him, he cared for him, he kept him as the pupil of his eye” (Deu 32:10). Hebrews calls the angels “ministering spirits sent out to serve for the sake of those who are to inherit salvation” (Heb 1:14). From the verses: the surrounding that men see is not all there is; God's care for those who fear him is carried out by his angels, unseen, and is stronger than what surrounds them.

Moses promised Israel that in the land Yahweh would “give you rest from all your enemies all around, and you will dwell in safety” (Deu 12:10). It was given in part under Joshua (Jos 21:44), under David (2Sa 7:1) and most fully under Solomon, the “man of rest”, of whom Yahweh said “I will give him rest from all his enemies all around … and I will give peace and quietness to Israel in his days” (1Ch 22:9; 1Ki 5:18). It did not last: Israel went after the gods of the peoples around them, and was sold into the hand of its enemies all around (Jdg 2:12, 14), until Jerusalem was a reproach to all around her (Dan 9:16). The prophets speak of the rest again, as still to come: Israel gathered from all around to its own soil (Ezk 37:21), dwelling in safety “when I execute judgments on all who despise them around them” (Ezk 28:26); Yahweh “a wall of fire all around” Jerusalem and “glory in her midst” (Zec 2:9); Jerusalem “a cup of reeling to all the peoples all around” (Zec 12:2); and Yahweh sitting in the valley of Jehoshaphat “to judge all the nations all around” (Jol 4:12), after which “Yahweh will be king over all the earth” (Zec 14:9). From the verses: the rest from all around that Solomon's reign showed for a time is promised to Israel in its own land, in a kingdom on the earth with Jerusalem at its centre, when Yahweh judges the nations around her.

note: Drafted 2026-11-15. Root key סבב, as BDB files the words and as the corpus keys them; no other entry has it. Words and BDB keys: סָבִיב o.ad.ac, סָבַב o.ad.aa, מֵסַב o.ad.ad, סִבָּה o.ad.ab, נְסִבָּה o.ad.af, מוּסָב o.ad.ae. The zero-token cross-references m.az.ag (מוּסַב), m.cp.ao (מֵסַב) and n.dr.ah (נֶסִבָּה) are left out. No personal name is formed from the root, so there are no name entries. סָבִיב is given pos adverb (its commonest use); its prepositional and noun uses are senses. Psa 140:10 מְסִבָּי is filed by the brief under מֵסַב (o.ad.ad) though tagged as a hiphil participle; it is kept there and the summary says so. Stems: the brief's “poel” (12 tokens) is kept as poel; the one piel is 2Sa 14:20. The verb's sense of sitting round a meal rests on 1Sa 16:11 and Sng 1:12 only and is given as an example under “go round”, not as a sense of its own. No Biblical Aramaic or Peshitta word: the brief finds none, and the Targum's verb for סָבַב is סְחַר (Jastrow s.v.). Cognates: Segert has the Ugaritic root only in the grammar (p. 73), not in the glossary; DULAT s.v. sb(b) not consulted. Krahmalkov p. 338 and Biella p. 325 read from the extracted text, PDFs not rendered. Arabic sabab and Sabaic sb are recorded as possible and named only on the “bring about / turn of events” senses; if they are judged not cognate, those senses rest on kin alone. Leads not followed: Akkadian šibbu “belt” (Oracc armep x000124750), compared by Klein, has š where Hebrew has s and is left out; Akkadian sabābu not found in Oracc; CAL for Aramaic סבב and Syriac not consulted. Greek: only κυκλόω, κύκλῳ and κυκλόθεν are recorded; the Septuagint's ἀποστρέφω, ἐπιστρέφω and στρέφω for the “turn” senses have no New Testament passage expounding a verse of this root and are left out; the מֵסַב → κύκλῳ locator is taken from the brief's totals, not from a single verse. Open questions for review: (1) Jer 31:22, “a female shall encompass a man”, is listed under the poel “encompass” with no interpretation; (2) the kingdom-of-god and angels doctrine items are reasoned conclusions; Luk 21:20 and Rev 20:9 are cited under κυκλόω without a doctrinal statement; (3) whether סָבִיב should be split into adverb and preposition words; (4) מוּסָב in Ezk 41:7 is not fixed by its verse.
